title.narrative: Inclusive Community Engagement for Humanitarian Response Prioritization in Baydhaba District.

description.narrative: ltpgtURRO will implement a Community Engagement (CE) exercise in Baydhaba District to conduct a structured, evidence-based needs assessment that ensures humanitarian interventions are guided by the priorities and voices of crisis-affected communities. The exercise will produce a district-level Community Engagement Plan (CEP) for Baydhaba, outlining ranked and costed priorities jointly developed with Area-Based Committee (ABC) members, OCHA, and other implementing partners (IPs). The CEP will include disaggregated participation data by age, gender, disability, and minority status, offering practical guidance for inclusive, equitable, and data-driven humanitarian programming. The project will also strengthen participatory planning processes by empowering ABCs and IPs to facilitate locally led decision-making that ensures the sustained inclusion of marginalized and minority groups in humanitarian response. lt/pgtltpgtThe CE exercise will begin with training for URRO staff and two ABC members from Baydhaba, facilitated by SHF and ASEP, one of the CE partners. These trained members will subsequently cascade the training to other URRO staff and ABC coordination group members to build consistent capacity across all levels. This will be followed by a three-day community entry and initial engagement phase, during which URRO, ABC, and IP representatives will introduce the project, build trust, and align expectations with participating communities. This phase will also support the selection of diverse community representatives across gender, age, and social groups, while mapping key actors, local governance structures, and access dynamics within the target areas. Building on this foundation, a ten-day participatory engagement exercise will be conducted across the selected villages, led by URRO’s Community Engagement Officer, URRO staff, the Programme Manager, and five ABC and IP representatives. Participatory methods including Participatory Rural Appraisal (PRA) tools such as community mapping and seasonal calendars will be used to capture community-defined priorities and perspectives. Before fieldwork, all URRO staff will undergo a five-day pre-field training led by URRO, covering ethical data collection, informed consent, confidentiality, inclusion, PSEA, and the use of Kobo Toolbox for real-time digital data entry and analysis. The data collected will be jointly analyzed by URRO, ABC members, and IP representatives, with priorities compiled, ranked, and costed using scorecards based on criteria such as urgency, severity, feasibility, and potential impact. The district-specific CEP will then be validated with ABCs and community representatives to ensure inclusivity, ownership, and practical alignment with local priorities. Throughout the process, ethical and protection principles including PSEA integration, participation of persons with disabilities, and engagement of marginalized groups will be upheld. Following the initial CE exercise, URRO will conduct six monthly community engagement sessions with the same community groups that participated in the development of the CEPs. These sessions will provide a platform for communities to reflect on progress, assess the implementation of agreed priorities, identify emerging needs, and strengthen accountability through regular dialogue and feedback. Each session will be facilitated by the Community Engagement Officer, supported by URRO staff, the Programme Manager, and Area-Based Committee (ABC) members, jointly covering the ten target villages: October Village, Ahmed Gurey, Busley Village, Reydabaale, Bakaro, Laan Buule, Awdiinle, El-Cadow, Goofgaduud Buurey Haraaw, and Ashagow. The Protection Officer will also participate in every session to ensure that Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Gender-Based Violence (GBV), and Child Protection (CP) considerations are systematically integrated into the discussions. ltbrgtlt/pgt
